newsitem.title: THAILAND: Hoechst says to float HMR unit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst says to float HMR unit in 1997.

text.p: German conglomerate Hoechst AG expects to float shares of its pharmaceutical subsidiary Hoechst Marion Roussel (HMR) in the second half of 1997, Hoechst board member Horst Waesche said on Thursday.
"We are in the process of preparing for the carve out of the pharmaceutical activities, HMR," Waesche told Reuters in an interview.

"We have of course to get the approval of the shareholders which will most likely be tabled for the next shareholders meeting in May. Following a positive decision we can expect it in the later part of next year, the second half of next year."
"We will retain a strong majority, a very strong majority of the shares," Waesche said.
He said about 20 percent of the company would be on offer with the shares listed on the Frankfurt and New York bourses, if the process goes according to plan.

He said the company may seek to remove non-core subsidiaries from the group, but said other flotations are currently unlikely. He said the group's policy was to make the entities more manageable and responsive to fast changing markets.
Describing Hoechst's corporate restructuring over the last year as a first step, Waesche said the company was currently satisfied with its structure.
